title: ToolManifest
description: A tool manifest: how a launcher discovers, configures, launches, and monitors one tool.

$schema.description: Optional reference to this schema, for editor validation. Ignored by the launcher.

formic.description: Manifest schema version. v1 is the only version this schema accepts.

name.description: Stable machine-readable tool identifier, unique per discovery source.

title.description: Human-readable display name shown in a launcher's tool list.

description.description: One-line description of what the tool does.

launch.description: How the launcher runs the tool.

command.description: The executable to run. May contain placeholder tokens, substituted like those in launch.args.

args.description: Argv passed to command. May contain {spec}/{repo}-style placeholder tokens the launcher substitutes; tokens are substituted in launch.command, launch.args and launch.cwd, never in env values.

cwd.description: Working directory the command runs in. May contain a {repo}-style placeholder token, substituted like those in launch.args.

config.description: What the tool reads for per-repo configuration.

schema.description: Path to a JSON Schema the launcher renders a config form from.

files.description: Files this tool reads, shown to the user for reference only: never parsed, resolved or opened by the launcher. Absolute paths and paths outside the source root are allowed.

status.description: How the launcher observes run status. Omitted entirely means the launcher falls back to exit-code monitoring.

kind.description: exit-code is the mandatory fallback every tool supports implicitly; ndjson and logfile are opt-in richer status channels.

fd.description: Which stream the ndjson status events are read from. Only meaningful when kind is ndjson.

events.description: The event kinds this tool's status stream may emit.

health.description: How the launcher checks the tool is installed/runnable before offering it.

check.description: Argv of a command that exits 0 when the tool is healthy.

pane.description: How the launcher should host this tool's terminal output.

prefer.description: The launcher's preferred hosting strategy for this tool.

interactive.description: true = this tool needs a real TTY and must never be run in a captured pane.

env.description: Environment variables this tool reads, so a launcher knows which keys to set and which are secrets, without guessing from source.

description.description: What this variable controls and why a launcher user would set it.

secret.description: true = a launcher must treat the value as a secret (never logged, never shown in plain UI).

required.description: true = the tool cannot run without this variable resolving to a value.

default.description: The value the tool falls back to when this variable is unset.

options.description: Enumerated values this variable accepts. Present and non-empty: a launcher renders the row as a chooser instead of free text. An empty list means no options (free text).

outputs.description: Where this tool's produced artifacts land.

evidenceDir.description: The name of an `env` entry above whose resolved value is the directory this tool writes its evidence into.

exit.description: This tool's exit codes and what each one means, keyed by the code as a decimal string.

needs.description: Things this tool requires before it can run: a secret, a provider gate, a runtime, a network policy, or a running service. Resolved against the machine's equip file before launch.

inputs.description: Named per-run inputs this tool accepts, substituted as {name} tokens into launch.command, launch.args and launch.cwd.

arguments.description: Launch arguments this tool accepts, stored per repo as modifiers in the profile's args list and appended after launch.args. Never asked per run (see inputs); never changes launch.command.

actions.description: Named actions over this one tool. Absent: the manifest is one implicit action (launch as declared). Present: a launcher shows the actions as a menu and launches one by name; launch supplies the shared command, cwd and argv prefix.

lifecycle.description: task (default): the tool runs and exits. service: the launched process is the long-running service. Applies to a manifest with no actions[]; an action declares its own.

launchOverride.description: Replaces launch.command, launch.args or launch.cwd on one operating system (darwin, linux or windows, matched against the launcher's host). Each key it sets replaces the base key; a key it omits keeps the base value. Tokens are substituted as in the base launch.

command.description: The executable to run on this operating system.

args.description: Argv passed to command on this operating system.

cwd.description: Working directory on this operating system.

healthOverride.description: Replaces health.check on one operating system (darwin, linux or windows, matched against the launcher's host).

check.description: Argv of the health command on this operating system.

option.description: One enumerated value an env entry or argument accepts.

value.description: The value itself, exactly as it is stored or passed.

description.description: What choosing this value does, shown beside it in a chooser.

argument.description: One launch argument a tool accepts. Serialized into the profile's args list: kind flag emits the flag alone when chosen; kind value and kind choice emit the flag, then its value.

flag.description: The flag exactly as it is passed on the command line, e.g. --healer.

description.description: What this argument does, shown beside it in a launcher's customize form.

kind.description: flag: the flag alone when chosen. value: the flag followed by a free-text value. choice: the flag followed by one of options.

options.description: The values a choice argument accepts; a choice with none is refused by doctor. Unused by the other kinds.

default.description: A value a launcher form prefills when none is saved. Only a prefill, never added at launch unless saved into the profile; ignored for kind flag.

action.description: One action a launcher may run over this tool.

name.description: Unique within the manifest; the second word of `formic launch <tool> <action>`.

command.description: Set: this action stands alone, with its own executable and argv (launch.args are not prefixed); cwd is inherited from launch unless set. Unset: launch.command, with args appended to launch.args. Placeholders are substituted as in launch.

args.description: Appended to launch.args (or the whole argv after command, when command is set). Placeholders are substituted.

arguments.description: This action's own declared arguments, after the manifest-level arguments; a flag declared at both levels is refused.

confirm.description: A sentence a launcher asks y/N before running; a non-interactive launch needs an explicit yes.

interactive.description: true = needs a real terminal (never captured). Unset: inherits pane.interactive.

exit.description: This action's exit codes and their meanings, keyed by the code as a decimal string; a code it does not list falls back to the manifest-level exit.

lifecycle.description: task (default) or service. A launcher opens a service action in its own tab.

whenUp.description: What to do when the tool's live probe already answers (up, or idle): skip, or launch anyway.

live.description: How a launcher asks whether this tool's service is up. The probe, whenUp and ready here serve a manifest with no actions[]; an action declares its own whenUp and ready.

probe.description: Exactly one probe kind: http, tcp or command. A command probe exiting 0 reports up.

idleExit.description: A command probe exiting with this code reports idle: the service answers but has nothing running. Exit 0 is still up; any other code is down.

ready.description: How long a launcher waits for a freshly started service to answer its probe (up, or idle), after a task exits 0 or after a service is spawned. The wait never changes the run's own outcome or exit code.

need.description: One thing a tool requires before it can run.

name.description: The secret's name, as recorded in the machine's equip file.

class.description: The need class this gate answers, e.g. browser.

env.description: The declared env[] entry that receives the chosen provider's name.

providers.description: The provider names this tool accepts for this gate.

name.description: The runtime this tool needs installed, e.g. docker.

policy.description: The network policy this tool needs in effect, e.g. privacy-vpn.

tool.description: An admitted tool whose live probe must be up (or idle). A launcher checks it before launching and refuses when it is not.

action.description: Which of that tool's actions meets this need.

input.description: One named per-run input a tool accepts.

name.description: The input's name; substituted as a {name} token in launch.command, launch.args and launch.cwd.

label.description: Human-readable label shown when prompting for this input.

kind.description: The input's value kind. An open string in this version.

required.description: true = the mission/launch cannot proceed without this input resolving to a value.

sensitive.description: true = the value must never be written to a durable run row or logged.
